verdict: Strong work; the Day 248 file is the best of the three, and its "the multi-summand obstruction was a *representation* artefact" diagnosis is the kind of result that collapses a machinery into something provable. The proved/computed boundary is drawn in the right place, with two adjustments: **Lemma T moves up to `proved`** (re-derived cold and exactly as Lemma H, and I verified its alternant foundation independently -- Lemma A 8/8, Cor. A1 6/6, from the definitions rather than his scripts), and **`lambda, mu in G` should be relabelled a hypothesis of the *route*, not of the theorem** (it is exactly the closure of L3''s "clean" condition under `lambda -> lambda^-`; certifier v2 reaches every allowed triple at N <= 7 without it). Corollary Delta independently confirmed, n <= 7, every c in [-8, 2n+8], both parities and both directions. The `allowed` domain is now machine-resolvable and all three of his census sizes reproduce exactly from his text alone (39/25, 762/408, 11360/5578); the Day 246 parity hole is structurally excluded, because the lower inclusion [0,2N-4] is now Proposition Z -- a proof over all parities -- and not a census. Motegi's biorthogonality is **corroborated**, not merely cited: I verified it first-hand 336/336 against my own symmetrisation engine, a different mechanism from his branching+RTV route; the residual is that **RTV stable-envelope uniqueness is unread by both of us and now sits under three results, two graded `proved`**. One new result offered back: **Day 248's Lemma A reaches the lambda side**, which is sharp-file Gap 1 -- the F-twist on a consecutive block is arithmetic of slope -1, his own Theorem B identity is its r=2 case, and in the constant-twist representative L3''s tie across the top block collapses to a single extremal head (verified on both of his named obstruction examples; exactly 1 for s >= 2, one head/tail tie left at s = 1). If that holds, `G` is removable and the upper end is `proved` for all N. That is Q532, and it is his to take.
